text:
# Etymology and Historical Names

Kadikoy was formerly known as Chalcedon during ancient and Byzantine periods. The current name, adopted after the 1453 Ottoman conquest, translates to 'Village of the Judge', referencing the jurisdiction granted to Istanbul's first judge, Hizir Bey.

# Ancient Settlement

Archaeological evidence indicates continuous habitation since prehistoric times, with relics dating to 5500-3500 BC found at the Fikirtepe Mound. Greeks from Megara established Chalcedon as their first Bosphorus settlement in 685 BC, several years before founding Byzantium across the strait.

# Medieval and Ottoman Periods

The Council of Chalcedon convened there in 451 AD as a significant ecclesiastical gathering. Ottoman control began in 1353, over a century before Constantinople's fall. Following the 1453 conquest, Chalcedon transitioned from rural settlement to market center.

# Modern Development

Kadikoy separated administratively from Uskudar in 1928, establishing its current district status.

# Cultural Character

The district emerged as the liberal cultural centre of the Anatolian side of Istanbul, distinguished by its concentration of bookshops, cinemas, bars, and cafes. It ranks first nationally on the Human Development Index among Turkish districts.

# Religious Diversity

Kadikoy historically housed populations representing Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. The Metropolis of Chalcedon remains headquartered there as one of four surviving metropolises within the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople.
